input.summary: Fix Query.one_of so a generator (any one-shot iterator) is materialised into a list once, when the query is built, so every document is tested against the full set of values and the query is reusable.
input.approach: In `Query.one_of` (tinydb/queries.py:476), add a step before building the test: `if isinstance(items, Iterator): items = list(items)`. `Iterator` is imported from `collections.abc`, which is already imported on line 20, so there is no new dependency. Generators, `map()`, `filter()` and `iter(...)` objects are all Iterators. They are the one-shot objects that get exhausted by the per-document `value in items`. Lists, tuples, sets, ranges and dict views are not Iterators and are left untouched, so list behaviour stays identical (FR-QUERY-002). The closure `lambda value: value in items` and the hash `('one_of', self._path, freeze(items))` then both use the materialised list. The hash therefore encodes the actual allowed values (a tuple after `freeze`) instead of the identity of a generator object. This keeps C2 and ADR-3 correct: two generators with different contents get different hashes, and the same query reused in several searches gives the same result (FR-QUERY-003). An empty generator becomes `[]`, which matches nothing (FR-QUERY-004). Also widen the type hint to `Iterable[Any]` and fix the docstring (Q-002 option a). The order of the generated values has no effect because membership is order-independent (AC-4).

alternatives.why_not: It changes the hash and behaviour for sets, which freeze() currently turns into a frozenset. It also copies the list on every call. The Iterator-only check keeps current behaviour for every non-one-shot input.

alternatives.option: Materialise lazily inside the test closure on first call (cache in a nonlocal)
alternatives.why_not: It is more code and adds mutable state. The hash would still have to be computed at build time, either from the generator's identity (wrong under C2/ADR-3) or by consuming it anyway.

alternatives.option: Leave the generator as is and mark one_of as list-only (docs/type change only)
alternatives.why_not: The docstring promises 'list or generator' and the issue is a bug report. The requirements say to fix the behaviour (ASM-003).

alternatives.option: Fix `freeze()` in utils.py to consume iterators
alternatives.why_not: It changes a shared helper used by every query. The test closure would still use the exhausted generator, so it does not fix the bug alone, and it has wider blast radius.

files.purpose: Materialise one-shot iterators passed to Query.one_of so all documents are matched against the full set of values, and hash the materialised values.

ac_mapping.test_idea: TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage) with tags a,b,a,c; search(Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])) equals [a,b,a].
Build q with a generator and call it on 'value 1', 'value 2', 'value 1' in turn; all three return True.
Generator query called on {'key1':'value 3'} returns False.
Docs b,a,a and a generator yielding 'a' then 'b'; search returns all three in document order.
List query one_of(['value 1','value 2']) returns True, True, False for value 1, value 2, value 3.

Use the same generator-based query object in db.search twice (also with the cache cleared by an insert in between); both results equal [a,b]. Also check that two queries built from different generators have different hashes.
Query().tag.one_of(t for t in []) called on {'tag':'a'} returns False.

constraints.how_respected: one_of still goes through `_generate_test` and its hash still includes the 'one_of' tag, the path and all arguments. The hash is now built from the materialised values, not the identity of a one-shot generator.
The only new import is `Iterator` from `collections.abc`, which queries.py already imports from; there is no import of table.py or database.py.
Only the standard library (`collections.abc`) is used; no third-party dependency.
Not affected: storages are not touched.
Not affected: Table and `_update_table` are not touched.

risks: The generator is consumed when one_of is called, not at search time. Code that relied on lazy consumption (unlikely) changes behaviour, and the caller's generator is exhausted afterwards.
An infinite generator would now hang at query construction instead of silently giving wrong results.

Q-001, Q-002 and Q-003 are open (P2/P3) and are resolved by their defaults: reusable query, one-shot iterators handled in addition to generators, empty generator matches nothing. FR-QUERY-003 and FR-QUERY-004 are ASSUMPTION-ONLY; if the maintainer wants single-use semantics, FR-QUERY-003 would be wrong.
The spec's TERM-001 says 'generator' strictly, but the fix also covers map()/filter()/iter(). This is a harmless superset. Sets and ranges already work and are unchanged.
The type hint changes from `list[Any]` to `Iterable[Any]`, which needs `Iterable` imported from `collections.abc` (also stdlib). Check that the mypy plugin and the existing typing tests still pass.
